item.text:
**6B.1 | Tinubu in 2024**
Bottom line: **mixed, leaning positive on stated intent and some concrete welfare programs, but weakened by patronage, repression, and the fact that many benefits were announced amid severe hardship rather than demonstrated as broad relief.** The record shows real welfare-oriented policy moves, but also evidence that human welfare was not consistently treated as the overriding purpose of rule.

**Accepted claims**
- **President Tinubu Directs Expeditious Processing of Welfare Benefits, Demands Monthly KPI Reports** | State House | 2024-02-22 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/ | Tinubu explicitly told civil servants to prioritize welfare-related interventions, warned against delays that worsen vulnerability, and required monthly KPI reporting. This is direct evidence that human welfare was being framed as a governing priority, not just rhetorical garnish. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.8

- **With Good Governance and Commitment, We Must Overcome Old Subsidy Beneficiaries** | State House | 2024-03-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/with-good-governance-and-commitment-we-must-overcomee-old-subsidy-benificiaries-president-tinubu/ | Tinubu said the treasury must not be abused, tied subsidy reform to student loans, consumer credit, and social welfare, and said relief should be targeted with NIN data. This supports a programmatic, welfare-through-policy reading rather than pure patronage. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **In Detail: The Student Loan (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024** | State House | 2024-04-04 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/ | The administration cast student loans and skills development as a structural welfare intervention to expand access to higher education and human capital. This is strong evidence of welfare as a real policy objective, especially for lower-income students. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **President Tinubu Approves Takeoff of Consumer Credit Scheme** | State House | 2024-04-24 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-approves-takeoff-of-consumer-credit-scheme/ | Tinubu described consumer credit as a way to improve quality of life and social mobility by helping citizens finance homes, vehicles, education, and healthcare. That is direct welfare-oriented rhetoric with an actual policy instrument behind it. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **President Tinubu Launches National Resettlement Scheme For Conflict Victims** | State House | 2024-07-06 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/ | The government launched a resettlement scheme for displaced and conflict-affected communities, framing it as rehabilitation, reintegration, and “permanent solutions,” not temporary relief. This is one of the clearest concrete welfare items in the 2024 record. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **President Tinubu Launches Education Campaign, Sys no Child Should be Excluded from Learning** | State House | 2024-05-13 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/ | Tinubu endorsed women’s rights, girls’ education, anti-GBV policy, and inclusive education, saying these were essential to development. This supports a genuine welfare-and-capabilities agenda, especially for women and children. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8

- **President Tinubu Offers Scholarships, Housing to Families of Slain Soldiers** | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-offers-scholarships-housing-to-families-of-slain-soldiers/ | Tinubu ordered scholarships and housing support for families of slain soldiers and pushed rapid payment of benefits. This shows the presidency using the state to materially support bereaved families rather than treating them as symbolic props. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification | The World Bank said the reform package aimed to create fiscal space for public services and scale up support to vulnerable households. That is external validation that the administration’s economic program included welfare as a real, stated objective. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- **Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency** | BusinessDay | 2024-02-21 | https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/ | The appointment of Tinubu’s son-in-law to the Federal Housing Authority was widely criticized as nepotism. That cuts directly against the idea that welfare institutions were insulated from patronage or that public office was organized primarily around human need. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8

- **Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk | HRW said authorities had failed to sustain measures for safe learning environments, leaving schoolchildren at continuing risk. This undercuts any broad claim that the administration had made child welfare a core, outcome-producing priority. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Nigeria: Girls Failed by Authorities After Escaping Boko Haram Captivity** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/ | Amnesty documented unlawful detention and weak reintegration support for girls and young women who escaped Boko Haram captivity. That is strong evidence that welfare for vulnerable survivors remained secondary or badly implemented. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Nigeria: Authorities Must Uphold Human Rights Ahead of Planned Nationwide Protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-08-01 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/08/nigeria-authorities-must-uphold-human-rights-ahead-of-planned-nationwide-protests/ | Amnesty warned authorities not to demonize protesters or use the planned protests as a pretext to crack down on rights. This is relevant because the protests were driven by food shortages and the cost-of-living crisis, showing welfare grievances were being treated as a security problem. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.8

- **Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #Endbadgovernance protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/ | Amnesty said police killed at least 24 protesters, detained over 1,200, and targeted people who supported protests on social media, while the protests themselves were about corruption and economic hardship. This is strong evidence that when welfare grievances surfaced, the state often answered with coercion rather than welfare-first accountability. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9, 3B.4

- **4 Nigerian journalists charged with cybercrime, defamation over fraud investigation** | CPJ | 2024-02-09 | https://cpj.org/2024/02/4-nigerian-journalists-charged-with-cybercrime-defamation-over-fraud-investigation/ | Police charged journalists who reported on corruption, which chills scrutiny of who captures public resources. That weakens the claim that the state was centered on human welfare rather than protecting insiders. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.7, 5B.8

- **Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting** | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/ | CPJ reported continued use of cybercrime charges against journalists even after reforms. This suggests a punitive information environment, which is bad evidence for a welfare-first governing ethic because it suppresses bad-news reporting about public harms. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **President Tinubu: I have no Cabal or Sponsors to Compensate** | State House | 2024-07-26 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-i-have-no-cabal-or-sponsors-to-compensate/ | Tinubu denied owing any cabal or sponsors and emphasized welfare measures like ward-level social support, student loans, consumer credit, and minimum-wage increases. The welfare language is real, but the need to rebut patronage claims shows how easily the administration’s welfare posture could be read as political defense rather than pure moral commitment. | IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence of **welfare-oriented promises and several concrete programs**, but less direct evidence of **measured outcomes** showing that welfare became the organizing core of rule across the whole state.
- The strongest negative evidence is not that Tinubu never talked about welfare, but that welfare was often pursued alongside or after **nepotism, protest suppression, and information-control behavior**.
- So the best calibrated read is: **Tinubu did treat human welfare as a real governing theme in 2024, but the record does not show it was consistently primary over patronage, coercion, and crisis management.**
